# Decode hex ports from /proc/net/tcp to check if port 3003 (0xBBB) is actually listening
python3 -c "
import socket, struct
ports_seen = set()
with open('/proc/net/tcp') as f:
    for line in f.readlines()[1:]:
        parts = line.strip().split()
        local = parts[1]
        state = parts[3]
        addr, port = local.split(':')
        port_dec = int(port, 16)
        ip_int = int(addr, 16)
        ip = socket.inet_ntoa(struct.pack('<I', ip_int))
        ports_seen.add((ip, port_dec, state))

# State 0A = LISTEN
print('Listening sockets (state=0A):')
for ip, port, state in sorted(ports_seen, key=lambda x: x[1]):
    if state == '0A':
        print(f'  {ip}:{port}')
print()
print('Port 3003 (0xBBB) present?', any(p == 3003 for _, p, _ in ports_seen))
print('Port 3000 (0xBB8) present?', any(p == 3000 for _, p, _ in ports_seen))
"
